text:
ashley: FYI — Customer 'AcmeHealth' hit repeated 400 errors when calling /invoke with our tool-calling path. They also saw a burst of 500s and latency spikes after the errors.

mike: Can you paste the request and the exact error?

ashley: Root message from their logs: 
```
POST /v1/invoke HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-2",
  "input": "summarize patient notes",
  "tool": "billing_lookup",
  "args": {
    "patient_id": 12345,
    "debug": true,
    "billing_profile": { "plan": "enterprise" },
    "session": null
  }
}
```

support-bot: Response: 400 Bad Request {
  "error": "func_schema",
  "message": "request rejected: additionalProperties \"billing_profile\" not allowed"
}

mike: That looks like our function schema set additionalProperties: false and session is non-nullable in the compiled schema. Why is session null here? It should be optional.

kevin: I see two issues: (1) schema migration we pushed yesterday tightened additionalProperties for the billing tool; (2) a compatibility layer should coerce nullable session but maybe the shim didn't run due to a route-level fast-fail when additionalProperties present.

jess: Customer also reports tokens billed even though call failed. Billing trace shows token usage charged at request time before validation.

ashley: Repro steps from customer (they gave us this exact curl):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/invoke \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-2","input":"x","tool":"billing_lookup","args":{"patient_id":12345,"billing_profile":{"plan":"enterprise"},"session":null}}'
```
If I remove billing_profile it succeeds (but they need it).

mike: Can you include the function schema we compiled for billing_lookup?

ashley: Pasted schema snippet from runtime: 
```
{
  "name": "billing_lookup",
  "params": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "patient_id": { "type": "integer" },
      "session": { "type": "object", "properties": { "id": {"type":"string"} }, "required": ["id"] }
    },
    "required": ["patient_id"],
    "additionalProperties": false
  }
}
```

ink: (reaction) :eyes:

kevin: Ah — session is defined but required.id is required, and session itself isn't marked nullable or optional. That explains null failing. Also additionalProperties:false blocks billing_profile. This was an intentional schema strictness change but it wasn't announced to support.

mike: For workaround we can: (A) allow additionalProperties on that function for a patch rollout, (B) accept unknown keys at the router-level and strip them before schema validation, or (C) coerce null session to omit session. Which is fastest?

kevin: Quickest is to add a lightweight pre-validate sanitization that strips unknown top-level keys in args before hitting the function schema. I'll push a hotfix branch to try. But note: that won't fix billing charge timing. We need to stop charging before schema validation succeeds.

jess: Billing workaround: we can issue a credit for failed requests in the customer's invoice while we patch. Also we should move token accounting to post-validation or mark flagged requests so billing can ignore them for now. I've flagged an urgent billing ops ticket.

ashley: Customer asked for root cause timeline and next steps. SRE status?

incidents-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-7883 — schema-hotfix-billing-30m

kevin: Plan: 1) Deploy a router pre-validator that strips additional properties for function args (hotfix) — ETA 30m. 2) Patch function schema generator to allow nullable session and add tests — ETA next deploy. 3) Billing: jess to credit affected requests and work with ops to ignore these failures for charge window.

mike: For traceability, please add the failing request IDs and sample logs to the incident ticket. Also add a regression test that sends args with extra keys and null session.

ashley: I added sample request IDs and attached the curl to the incident. Customer accepted provisional credit and wants ETA. I'll update them after hotfix.

kevin: Hotfix pushed to canary. Quick verification: sanitized request now becomes: 
```
{"patient_id":12345}
```
and passes schema validation. Confirming no more 400.

ashley: Customer confirms immediate success against canary endpoint, will test at scale. Thanks. :relieved:

jess: Billing team applied provisional credit for 42 failed calls. Will reconcile after root cause is fully resolved.

mike: Follow-ups: add a telemetry flag so we can detect requests that were "stripped" by pre-validator, and ensure we don't reintroduce the strict additionalProperties:false without a migration plan.

ashley: Noted. Closing loop with customer in 2h once stable.

support-bot: Thread archived to incident #INC-2026-7883.
